assignment:
Your principal is reconsidering the school's cell phone policy. She is considering two possible policies: 
Policy 1: Allow students to bring phones to school and use them during lunch periods and other free times, as long as the phones are turned off during class time. 
Policy 2: Do not allow students to have phones at school at all.
Write a letter to your principal convincing her which policy you believe is better. Support your position with specific reasons.
essay_1:
Dear Principal,

I think you should choose Policy 1. It lets students bring phones to school and use them at lunch and other free periods, as long as the phones stay off during class. A full ban sounds simple, but it is a bad idea. Students like their phones, and taking them away at the door teaches nothing useful.

First, phones help students stay in touch with their families. Many kids have parents who work late, brothers or sisters at other schools, or a ride home that changes at the last minute. A phone lets a student confirm a pickup, call a parent after a scary moment, or tell family they are safe. Under Policy 2, those students would have no easy way to reach home during the school day, and that is a serious problem.

Second, a ban only hides phones. Students would stash devices in bags, bathrooms, and lockers, and all that sneaking would be worse than a few minutes of scrolling at lunch. Policy 1 is a clear rule that is easy to follow: phones away in class, free time outside it.

Third, free time is when students hang out, read the news, or check their schedules. Those are useful habits. Keeping phones in pockets during lunch lets students pick how to spend their break, and it shows that we can be trusted to act responsibly.

Finally, schools should teach students how to handle their devices, not just hide the problem. Policy 1 gives teachers a fine chance to talk about phone rules in class, talk with students about screen habits, and step in when a phone gets distracting. A total ban shuts that conversation down before it starts, but a clear plan keeps it open.

For these reasons, I believe Policy 1 is the better choice. It keeps students close to their families, it is easier to enforce than a ban that students will dislike and sneak around, and it helps us learn to use technology with good judgment. I hope you will say yes, because this would make our school a calmer and more trusting place.

Respectfully,

A Student
essay_2:
Dear Principal,

I think we should pick Policy 1. That policy lets students bring phones to school and use them at lunch and during free periods, but phones have to stay off during class. I know a full ban seems easier to do, and I get why people like it. But if we make kids leave their phones at the door, we never learn how to use them the right way, and that is something we will need for the rest of our lives.

First, phones help students stay in touch with their families. A lot of kids have parents who work late, or brothers and sisters at a different school, or a ride home that changes at the last minute. My friend missed the bus one time and had to call her mom from the front office. She could only do that because she had her phone. Under Policy 2, kids like her would have no real way to reach home during the day.

Second, a ban does not make phones go away. It just hides them. People would stick phones in their bags, in the bathroom, or in their lockers. Everybody would spend more time sneaking around than they would spend on their phones at lunch. Policy 1 is a simple rule that is easy to understand. Phones are away in class and free to use outside of it, so nobody has to guess.

Third, free time is when most students talk to friends, check the news, or look up their schedule. Those things are normal. If phones stay in our pockets during lunch, kids can choose how to spend their break. It also shows the school trusts us to act responsibly instead of treating us like we are going to cause trouble.

Finally, I think the school should teach us how to manage our phones instead of just taking them away. With Policy 1, teachers can talk to us about phone rules in class. They can talk about how much screen time is too much, and they can step in when a phone is distracting someone. A total ban shuts down that conversation before it can even start, and then nobody learns anything about it.

So I think Policy 1 is the better choice. It keeps students connected to their families, and it is easier to enforce than a ban that people will just work around. It also helps us get ready to use technology with good judgment. I hope you will think about it and talk with the other teachers before you decide.

Respectfully,

A Student
